properties.WarningTitle: STAY INFORMED - Garbutt and Belgian Gardens - fire as at 2:17pm Monday, 27 July 2026
properties.CallToAction: Stay Informed
properties.WarningText:
A fire is burning near Peel Street and Sunderland Street, Garbutt.

Stay informed because the situation could change.

What you should do:

- Check for warning updates often and listen to your local radio station.

- Decide what you will do if the bushfire gets closer.

- If the smoke is thick where you are, stay inside and close windows and doors.

- If you need medication to help you breathe keep it close. Smoke can make it hard to breathe.

- Do not fly drones around the fire as they affect firefighting.

- If you are in danger, call Triple Zero (000) now.

Impacts:

- Some roads may be closed or impacted by smoke. It could be hard to see. You may need to drive a different way.

What firefighters are doing:

- Firefighters are working to control the fire.

More information:

- For all fire warnings, visit the Qld Fire website.

- Follow Queensland Fire Department on Facebook.

- For road closures, visit the QLD Traffic website or call 13 19 40.

- For local information visit your Council’s Local Disaster Dashboard.

- If you are worried about your health call your doctor or 13 HEALTH (13 432 584).

- Natural disasters can affect your mental health. If you need help contact:

  - Lifeline on 13 11 14.

  - Beyond Blue on 1300 224 636.

  - Kids Helpline on 1800 551 800.

- If you need translation, call TIS National on 131 450.

- Learn how to get ready for a bushfire on the Qld Fire website - Prepare - Bushfire.

Updates will be issued if the situation changes.

This warning is from the Queensland Fire Department.

properties.WarningTitle: AVOID SMOKE - Lakeland - fire as at 1:57pm Sunday, 26 July 2026
properties.CallToAction: Avoid Smoke
properties.WarningText:
Thick smoke is affecting Lakeland and Byerstown Range. This is from a large fire burning near Byerstown Range, Mulligan Highway.

Fire crews are currently on scene. This fire could burn for days. Protect yourself from the impacts of smoke.

What you should do:

- If the smoke is thick where you are, stay inside and close windows and doors.

- If you need medication to help you breathe keep it close.

- If you are worried about your health call your doctor or 13 HEALTH (13 432 584). If it is an emergency, call Triple Zero (000) now.

- If you are affected by the smoke you may need to leave the area.

- Check for warning updates often.

- Do not fly drones around the fire as they affect firefighting.

Impacts:

- No properties are at risk.

- Smoke could make it hard for some people to breathe and can cause health issues.

- Some roads may be closed or impacted by smoke. It could be hard to see. You may need to drive a different way.

More information:

- For all fire warnings, visit the Qld Fire website.

- Follow Queensland Fire Department on Facebook.

- For road closures, visit the QLD Traffic website or call 13 19 40.

- For local information visit your Council’s Local Disaster Dashboard.

- If you need translation, call TIS National on 131 450.

- Learn how to get ready for a bushfire on the Qld Fire website - Prepare - Bushfire.

Updates will be issued if the situation changes.

This warning is from the Queensland Fire Department.

properties.WarningTitle: AVOID SMOKE (HAZARD REDUCTION BURN) - Mount Nathan (Gold Coast) - fire as at 10:15am Monday, 27 July 2026
properties.CallToAction: Avoid Smoke (Hazard Reduction Burn)
properties.WarningText:
Thick smoke is affecting Mount Nathan, Clagiraba and surrounding areas. This is from hazard reduction burning in the Mount Nathan Reserve.

Protect yourself from the impacts of smoke.

At 2pm today a national test of a new alerting system, AusAlert, will be conducted by the Australian Government. Mobile devices will receive a notification and a loud siren-like sound will play for around 10 seconds. This test is unrelated to the fire in the Mount Nathan Reserve. For more information about the AusAlert national test go to ausalert.gov.au.

- If the smoke is thick where you are, stay inside and close windows and doors.
